children: US solar energy systems provider's Q3 revenue rose sequentially but fell 41% yr/yr on lower residential demand
Commercial revenue grew 20% yr/yr, partially offsetting residential decline
Net loss widened to $11.8 mln, including $9.8 mln in non-cash impairment charges
Company expects residential demand to remain sensitive to financing economics and tax credit expiration
SUNation continues to prioritize liquidity, cost management, and advancing the Suniva merger
Company is evaluating financing alternatives to support operations and maintain financial flexibility
RESIDENTIAL DEMAND DROP - Co said expiration of federal residential tax credit led to lower residential installation activity and a 41% yr/yr revenue decline
COMMERCIAL GROWTH - Commercial revenue rose 20% yr/yr, driven by New York projects, helping diversify revenue
COST REDUCTIONS - SG&A expense declined 37% yr/yr due to lower selling, marketing and personnel costs
